questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Spines** are not a component of a flower; they are modified leaves, stems, or stipules that are typically hard, pointed, and meant for protection.
 
• Flowers are reproductive structures in angiosperms (flowering plants) and typically consist of four main parts: androecium, corolla, calyx, and gynoecium.
 
• The primary role of spines is to protect the plant from herbivores and reduce water loss, especially in arid environments.
 
• Unlike the other options listed (androecium, corolla, and calyx), spines do not play a role in the reproductive process of the flower.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Androecium**

 
 
• The androecium is the collective term for the stamens in a flower. Each stamen typically consists of a filament and an anther, where pollen is produced.
 
• It is the male reproductive part of the flower.
 
 
 
• **Corolla**
 
 
• The corolla is the collective term for the petals of a flower.
 
• Petals are often brightly colored to attract pollinators.
 
 
 
• **Calyx**
 
 
• The calyx is the collective term for the sepals of a flower.
 
• Sepals are typically green and provide protection to the flower bud before it opens.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**
 
 
• The gynoecium is the collective term for the female reproductive parts of a flower, consisting of one or more carpels.
 
• Each carpel typically includes an ovary, style, and stigma.

questions.question: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Benaras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu College was established in the year 1791.
 
• It was founded in the city of Benaras, which is now known as Varanasi.
 
• The institution was set up to provide Western education to Indians.
 
• It played a significant role in the Indian Renaissance and the spread of modern education in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindu College:**

 
 
• The Hindu College in Benaras was one of the earliest institutions to provide a structured curriculum for Western-style education in India.
 
• It was founded by influential citizens of Benaras, including Raja Rammohan Roy.
 
• The college was established with the aim of imparting modern education in various fields such as science, mathematics, and the humanities.
 
• It later evolved into the Central Hindu School and eventually became a part of Banaras Hindu University (BHU).
 
 
 
• **Banaras Hindu University (BHU):**
 
 
• Established in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU is one of the largest residential universities in Asia.
 
• BHU offers courses in various fields including arts, science, engineering, medicine, and agriculture.
 
• The university is renowned for its research and academic excellence.
 
• It has a sprawling campus spread over 1,300 acres in Varanasi.
 
 
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy:**
 
 
• Raja Rammohan Roy was a prominent social and educational reformer in India during the early 19th century.
 
• He is often called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" due to his efforts in promoting modern education and social reforms.
 
• He was an advocate for the abolition of practices such as Sati and child marriage.
 
• His contributions laid the foundation for the development of modern Indian society.

questions.question: Where is the Gulf of Mannar located?

options.text: Between the south-eastern tip of India and the eastern coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the north-western coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the southern coast of Sri Lanka

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is a large shallow bay forming part of the Laccadive Sea in the Indian Ocean.
 
• It lies between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka, specifically between Tamil Nadu and the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.
 
• The Gulf of Mannar is renowned for its rich biodiversity and is home to the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, which is one of the richest coastal regions in Asia.
 
• This region is famous for its pearl banks and is often referred to as the Pearl of the Indian Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://www.worldatlas.com/r/w768/upload/fa/49/60/adobestock-516979692.jpeg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park**

 
 
• It is a protected area in the Gulf of Mannar and covers an area of about 560 square kilometers.
 
• The park is known for its coral reefs, seagrasses, and mangroves, which provide habitat for numerous marine species.
 
• It is home to endangered species such as the dugong, sea turtles, and various species of dolphins and whales.
 
• The park is part of the larger Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, which is recognized by UNESCO.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance**
 
 
• The Gulf of Mannar acts as a natural boundary between India and Sri Lanka.
 
• This region is historically significant as it has been a major trading route for centuries.
 
• The Mannar Island, located in the gulf, is known for its historical importance and natural beauty.
 
• The shallow waters and coral reefs make it a popular destination for marine research and ecotourism.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns**
 
 
• The region faces environmental challenges such as coral bleaching, overfishing, and pollution.
 
• Conservation efforts are in place to protect the unique marine biodiversity of the Gulf of Mannar.
 
• Local communities are involved in sustainable fishing practices to preserve the ecological balance.
 
• There are ongoing initiatives to promote awareness and education about marine conservation in the area.

questions.question: Who among the following won a Gold Medal at the 2021 World Cadet Wrestling Championship held in Budapest, Hungary?

• The event features various weight categories for both male and female wrestlers.
 
• The championship aims to provide a platform for young wrestlers to showcase their talent and gain international experience.
 
 
 
• **United World Wrestling (UWW)**
 
 
• UWW is the international governing body for the sport of wrestling, overseeing wrestling disciplines such as Freestyle, Greco-Roman, and Beach Wrestling.
 
• It was founded in 1912 and is headquartered in **Corsier-sur-Vevey, Switzerland**.
 
• UWW organizes various international competitions, including the World Wrestling Championships, Continental Championships, and the Olympic Games wrestling events.
 
• The organization is committed to promoting and developing the sport of wrestling globally, ensuring fair play and adherence to the rules.
 
 
 
• **Indian Wrestlers on the Global Stage**
 
 
• India has a rich history in wrestling, with the sport being one of the oldest and most popular in the country.
 
• Indian wrestlers have made significant strides on the international stage, winning medals in events such as the Olympics, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, and World Championships.
 
• Notable Indian wrestlers include **Sushil Kumar**, **Bajrang Punia**, **Vinesh Phogat**, and **Sakshi Malik**.
 
• The success of wrestlers like Priya Malik highlights the continued growth and potential of Indian wrestling on the global stage.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-tax revenue source for the government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fees and fines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Non-tax revenue** refers to the recurring income earned by the government from sources other than taxes.
 
• Fees and fines are common examples of non-tax revenue. **Fees** are payments made to the government for specific services or activities (e.g., passport fees, court fees), while **fines** are penalties imposed for violating laws or regulations.
 
• Non-tax revenue sources help the government fund its operations without increasing the tax burden on citizens.
 
• Other examples of non-tax revenue include **interest receipts** on loans given by the government, **dividends** from public sector enterprises, and income from government property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Personal income tax:**

 
 
• It is a **direct tax** levied on the income of individuals.
 
• The rate of personal income tax varies based on income slabs and is progressive in nature, meaning higher income earners pay a higher percentage in taxes.
 
 
 
• **Corporate income tax:**
 
 
• This is a tax imposed on the net income or profit of corporations.
 
• It is a significant source of revenue for the government and is also a direct tax.
 
 
 
• **Value-added tax (VAT):**
 
 
• VAT is an **indirect tax** levied on the value added to goods and services at each stage of production or distribution.
 
• Consumers ultimately bear the cost of VAT as it is included in the purchase price of goods and services.
 
 
 
• **Non-tax revenue sources:**
 
 
• These include all government revenue sources that do not fall under the category of taxes.
 
• Examples include fees for services, fines and penalties, dividends from public enterprises, interest receipts, and revenue from government properties.

questions.question: Sangeet Natak Akademy Awardee Sulochana Chavan was a famous _______ singer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lavani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sulochana Chavan was a legendary singer known for her contributions to the traditional Marathi folk genre of **Lavani music**.
 
• Lavani is a genre of music popular in Maharashtra and is noted for its powerful rhythm and sensuous, yet socially significant, lyrics.
 
• Lavani has traditionally been performed by female artists and is recognized for its combination of song and dance.
 
• Chavan's contributions to Lavani music earned her widespread acclaim and numerous accolades, including the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Giddha**

 
 
• Giddha is a popular folk dance of women in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.
 
• It is performed by women during special occasions and festivals, characterized by energetic movements and traditional Punjabi attire.
 
 
 
• **Jhumair**
 
 
• Jhumair is a traditional folk dance and song of the Chotanagpur plateau region in Jharkhand, India.
 
• It is performed during harvest season and other community celebrations, featuring slow rhythmic movements and traditional instruments.
 
 
 
• **Ghumar**
 
 
• Ghumar is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, India, performed by women in colorful attire.
 
• The dance is noted for its graceful circular movements and is performed during festive occasions like weddings and other celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Lavani**
 
 
• Lavani is a traditional folk art form that combines song and dance, originating from Maharashtra, India.
 
• The word 'Lavani' is derived from the Marathi word 'Lavanya', which means beauty, signifying the grace and charm of the performance.
 
• Lavani songs are known for their fast tempo and are often performed to the beats of the dholki drum.
 
• The dance is characterized by its vibrant costumes, energetic footwork, and expressive gestures.

questions.question: Which of the following plants is used to cure cold and cough?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tulsi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum)**, also known as Holy Basil, is a revered medicinal plant in India.
 
• It is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to treat **cold, cough, and other respiratory ailments**.
 
• Tulsi leaves are known to have **antibacterial, antiviral, and antifungal properties**, which help in relieving infections causing cold and cough.
 
• Consumption of Tulsi tea or Tulsi-infused water can **boost immunity and provide relief from respiratory disorders**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babool (Acacia nilotica)**

 
 
• Babool tree has various medicinal uses, including in dental care, skin care, and as a remedy for diarrhea and dysentery.
 
• Its bark and leaves are commonly used in traditional medicine.
 
 
 
• **Jamun (Syzygium cumini)**
 
 
• Jamun fruit and seeds are used in Ayurvedic medicine to manage diabetes.
 
• It is also beneficial for digestive health and in treating ulcers.
 
 
 
• **Arjun (Terminalia arjuna)**
 
 
• Arjun tree is well-known for its cardiovascular benefits.
 
• Its bark is used to treat heart diseases, hypertension, and cholesterol issues.

questions.question: Which is the colloquial term to describe the occurrence of pre-monsoon rains in India especially in parts of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mango showers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mango showers are the colloquial term used to describe pre-monsoon rains in India, particularly in Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• These showers usually occur between March and April and are known to aid the ripening of mangoes, which is why they are called "mango showers".
 
• They are also beneficial for other crops and help to mitigate the high temperatures experienced in the summer months.
 
• The showers are a result of thunderstorms caused by the confluence of moist air from the Indian Ocean and the Bay of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalbaisakhi**

 
 
• Kalbaisakhi, also known as Nor'westers, are violent thunderstorms that occur in the northeastern and eastern parts of India, particularly in West Bengal and Odisha.
 
• These storms are common in the pre-monsoon season, especially in the months of April and May.
 
• They are characterized by high-speed winds, heavy rain, and sometimes hail, which can cause significant damage to crops and property.
 
 
 
• **Nor Westers**
 
 
• Nor'westers are a type of storm that occurs in the northeastern and eastern parts of India, particularly in West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha.
 
• They are caused by the interaction of hot, dry air from the northwest with moist air from the Bay of Bengal.
 
• These storms can bring heavy rainfall, strong winds, and hail, often leading to damage in the affected areas.
 
 
 
• **Orange Showers**
 
 
• There is no widely recognized meteorological phenomenon known as "Orange showers".
 
• This term does not correspond to any specific weather pattern or event in India.

questions.question: The name ‘Piyadassi’ is associated with whom among the following Mauryan kings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Piyadassi** is a title which means "beloved of the gods" and it was used by Ashoka in his inscriptions.
 
• Ashoka was the third emperor of the Mauryan dynasty and is considered one of India's greatest rulers.
 
• Ashoka ruled from 268 to 232 BCE and his reign was marked by an extensive expansion of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and propagated the religion across Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mauryan Empire**

 
 
• The Mauryan Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE after overthrowing the Nanda dynasty.
 
• It was one of the largest empires in the world at its peak, spanning from modern-day Afghanistan to Bengal and south into the Deccan Plateau.
 
• Chandragupta was succeeded by his son Bindusara, who expanded the empire further before passing it to Ashoka.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly organized with a centralized government and a bureaucratic system.
 
 
 
• **Kalinga War**
 
 
• The Kalinga War was fought between the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka and the state of Kalinga around 261 BCE.
 
• This war is particularly significant because of the massive destruction and loss of life it caused.
 
• The aftermath of the war had a profound impact on Ashoka, leading him to embrace Buddhism and propagate peace and non-violence.
 
• Ashoka's transformation post-Kalinga War is well-documented in his rock and pillar edicts.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism**
 
 
• Buddhism is a religion and philosophy based on the teachings of Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) who lived in the 5th century BCE.
 
• Ashoka's patronage played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism across India and beyond.
 
• Ashoka convened the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) to discuss the teachings and spread of Buddhism.
 
• His efforts in promoting Buddhism included sending emissaries and missionaries to various parts of Asia, including Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, and Central Asia.

questions.question: The festival of 'Rath Yatra' of Puri in Odisha is dedicated to which deity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Jagannath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rath Yatra of Puri is dedicated to **Lord Jagannath**, who is considered a form of Lord Vishnu.
 
• This annual festival involves a grand procession where the deities are taken out of the Jagannath Temple and placed in chariots, symbolizing their journey to their aunt's house.
 
• The festival is celebrated with much pomp and grandeur, attracting millions of devotees from across the world.
 
• The festival generally occurs in the month of June or July, based on the Hindu lunar calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Jagannath:**

 
 
• Lord Jagannath is a deity worshipped primarily in the Indian state of Odisha.
 
• He is considered a form of Lord Vishnu, and is also identified with Krishna and Buddha.
 
• The Jagannath Temple in Puri is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites, which are considered very sacred by Hindus.
 
• The temple is famous for its annual Rath Yatra, or chariot festival, in which the three main deities are pulled on huge and elaborately decorated temple cars.
 
 
 
• **Rath Yatra:**
 
 
• The Rath Yatra involves the transportation of deities on large chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple, which is about 3 kilometers away.
 
• The three deities—Lord Jagannath, his brother Balabhadra, and sister Subhadra—are taken out in three separate chariots.
 
• The chariots are pulled by thousands of devotees who consider it an auspicious act.
 
• The festival lasts for nine days, and the return journey of the deities is known as Bahuda Yatra.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Rath Yatra symbolizes the journey of Lord Jagannath along with his siblings to their maternal aunt's house.
 
• It represents the idea of the divine coming down to meet the devotees, breaking the barriers of the temple.
 
• The festival promotes the spirit of brotherhood and unity among people, irrespective of their caste or creed.

questions.question: How many members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India has the authority to nominate **12 members** to the Rajya Sabha.
 
• These nominated members are chosen for their **expertise in various fields** such as literature, science, art, and social service.
 
• This provision is under **Article 80 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The purpose of these nominations is to ensure that the Rajya Sabha benefits from the experience and specialized knowledge of distinguished individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha**

 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• It represents the states and union territories of the country.
 
• The Rajya Sabha has a maximum membership of 250 members.
 
• Out of these, 238 members are elected by the states and union territories, while 12 are nominated by the President.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
 
 
• **Article 80 of the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• This article deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• It specifies the maximum number of members, the method of election, and the nomination of members by the President.
 
• Under this article, the President nominates 12 members who have special knowledge or practical experience in various fields such as literature, science, art, and social service.
 
 
 
• **Nominated Members**
 
 
• The nominated members bring diverse expertise to the Rajya Sabha.
 
• They are not bound by party lines and can contribute independently to debates and legislation.
 
• Some notable nominated members include Lata Mangeshkar (singer), Sachin Tendulkar (cricketer), and Raghunath Mohapatra (sculptor).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the socio-economic objective of Industrial Policy Statement 1980?

options.text: Consumer protection against high prices and bad quality
Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 emphasized **enhancing productivity, employment generation, and the optimum utilization of existing production capacity**.
 
• It aimed at the **promotion of export-oriented industries** to improve foreign exchange earnings.
 
• The policy also focused on **consumer protection against high prices and poor quality** of goods.
 
• **Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment (FDI)** was not a primary objective of the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Statement 1980**

 
 
• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 was introduced to revitalize the Indian economy and make it more competitive.
 
• The policy emphasized modernization, technological upgradation, and the development of small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
 
• It aimed at achieving higher growth rates and industrial diversification to reduce regional disparities.
 
• The policy also sought to improve the efficiency of public sector enterprises and increase their contribution to the economy.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**
 
 
• FDI involves investment from a foreign entity into the business interests of another country.
 
• It is a significant source of non-debt financial resources for the economic development of a country.
 
• FDI brings in capital, technology, and expertise, and can lead to job creation and infrastructure development.
 
• While FDI is important, it was not the main focus of the Industrial Policy of 1980, which was more oriented towards self-reliance and domestic industrial growth.

questions.question: Grignard reagent is represented as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CH₃-Mg-Cl**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Grignard reagents are organomagnesium compounds which are commonly represented as **R-Mg-X**, where R is an organic group and X is a halogen.
 
• In the given options, **CH₃-Mg-Cl** (Methylmagnesium chloride) fits this representation.
 
• Grignard reagents are highly reactive and are used in various organic synthesis reactions, particularly for forming carbon-carbon bonds.
 
• They were discovered by the French chemist Victor Grignard, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1912 for this discovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grignard Reagent:**

 
 
• Grignard reagents are typically prepared by reacting an alkyl or aryl halide with magnesium metal in an anhydrous ether solvent.
 
• They are strong nucleophiles and strong bases, making them very useful in organic chemistry for forming new carbon-carbon bonds.
 
• The general formula for a Grignard reagent is R-Mg-X, where R can be an alkyl, aryl, or vinyl group, and X is usually a halogen like chlorine, bromine, or iodine.
 
• Due to their high reactivity, Grignard reagents must be handled under an inert atmosphere (such as nitrogen or argon) to prevent them from reacting with moisture or oxygen in the air.
 
 
 
• **Victor Grignard:**
 
 
• François Auguste Victor Grignard was a French chemist who discovered the Grignard reagent, which revolutionized the field of organic chemistry.
 
• His discovery allowed for the formation of carbon-carbon bonds, which is fundamental in the synthesis of a wide variety of organic compounds.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1912 for this significant contribution.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Grignard Reagents:**
 
 
• Grignard reagents are used to form various types of carbon-carbon bonds, making them invaluable in the synthesis of alcohols, acids, and other organic compounds.
 
• They can react with carbonyl compounds (such as aldehydes and ketones) to form secondary and tertiary alcohols.
 
• They are also used in the synthesis of carboxylic acids by reacting with carbon dioxide.
 
• In addition to their use in academic research, Grignard reagents are also used in the pharmaceutical and chemical industries for the synthesis of complex organic molecules.

questions.question: Which of the following crops is NOT grown during the Zaid season in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rice is typically grown during the Kharif season (June to November) and Rabi season (November to March) in India.
 
• The Zaid season falls between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, specifically from March to June.
 
• Crops like cucumber, watermelon, and muskmelon are commonly grown during the Zaid season due to their shorter growing period and summer adaptability.
 
• Rice requires a significant amount of water and is usually grown in areas with assured irrigation during the monsoon season (Kharif) or post-monsoon season (Rabi).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Season**

 
 
• The Kharif season is also known as the monsoon season, running from June to November.
 
• Crops grown during this season are typically sown with the beginning of the first rains in July, during the south-west monsoon season, and harvested in October.
 
• Major Kharif crops include rice, maize, sorghum, pearl millet, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Rabi Season**
 
 
• The Rabi season is known as the winter season, running from November to March.
 
• Crops are sown in winter and harvested in the spring.
 
• Major Rabi crops include wheat, barley, peas, gram, and mustard.
 
 
 
• **Zaid Season**
 
 
• The Zaid season falls between the Kharif and Rabi seasons, specifically from March to June.
 
• Crops grown during this season have a shorter growing period and are typically summer crops.
 
• Examples of Zaid crops include cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, and bitter gourd.
 
 

This detailed solution provides comprehensive information about the correct option and explains the different agricultural seasons in India

questions.question: As per article 123, the ordinance making power is the most important legislative power of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The ordinance making power is a significant legislative power vested in the President of India.
 
• As per Article 123 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the authority to promulgate ordinances when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session.
 
• The ordinance holds the same force and effect as an act of Parliament.
 
• This power is intended to address urgent situations requiring immediate legislative action.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ordinance:**

 
 
• An ordinance is a temporary law enacted by the President of India on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
• It is promulgated when Parliament is not in session and immediate action is required.
 
• Ordinances must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembling, or they cease to operate.
 
• Ordinances allow the government to take swift action on matters of urgency without waiting for Parliament to convene.
 
 
 
• **Article 123 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Article 123 grants the President the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of Parliament.
 
• This provision ensures that the executive can address urgent issues without legislative delays.
 
• Ordinances must be laid before both Houses of Parliament and require their approval to become permanent laws.
 
• This power is subject to judicial review to prevent misuse and ensure adherence to constitutional principles.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution follows the principle of separation of powers among the executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• The President's ordinance-making power represents an overlap between the executive and legislative functions.
 
• This power is exercised with checks and balances to prevent abuse and ensure accountability.

questions.question: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1931**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on **5 March 1931** between Mahatma Gandhi and the then Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin.
 
• This pact marked the end of the **civil disobedience movement** led by the Indian National Congress against British rule in India.
 
• Under the terms of the pact, the British Government agreed to **release all political prisoners** who had been detained during the civil disobedience movement.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi, representing the Indian National Congress, agreed to **discontinue the civil disobedience movement** and participate in the **Second Round Table Conference** in London.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**

 
 
• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was a political agreement signed by Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin, in 1931.
 
• It was a significant event in the Indian freedom struggle, which led to the cessation of the civil disobedience movement that was initiated against the British Salt Tax.
 
• The pact included several concessions by the British Government, such as the withdrawal of all ordinances and prosecutions, release of prisoners arrested for participating in the salt march, and the return of confiscated properties of the satyagrahis.
 
• Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference in London as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement**
 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, the Civil Disobedience Movement aimed at disobeying certain laws, demands, and commands of the British government, particularly the Salt Act.
 
• The movement began with the Dandi March, where Gandhi and his followers marched to the Arabian Sea coast to produce salt from seawater in defiance of British laws.
 
• This movement attracted widespread participation from various sections of Indian society and was a crucial step towards India's independence.
 
• The movement saw significant government repression, including the arrest of thousands of protesters and leaders.
 
 
 
• **Second Round Table Conference**
 
 
• The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in September 1931 and was attended by Mahatma Gandhi as the representative of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The conference aimed to discuss constitutional reforms in India and the future governance of the country.
 
• Despite the discussions, the conference did not result in any significant agreements, leading to Gandhi's return to India and the resumption of the civil disobedience movement.
 
• The failure of the conference highlighted the deep divisions between the British authorities and Indian leaders regarding India's political future.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ampere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SI unit of electric current is the **Ampere**, symbolized as **A**.
 
• It is named after **André-Marie Ampère**, a French physicist and mathematician who is considered one of the founders of the science of classical electromagnetism.
 
• One Ampere is defined as the flow of one coulomb of charge per second.
 
• It is a fundamental unit in the International System of Units (SI), and it is used to quantify the amount of electric charge passing a point in an electric circuit per unit time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm (Ω)**

 
 
• The Ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
 
• Named after German physicist Georg Simon Ohm, it quantifies the resistance in a circuit.
 
• One Ohm is defined as the resistance between two points of a conductor when a constant potential difference of 1 Volt, applied to these points, produces a current of 1 Ampere.
 
 
 
• **Volt (V)**
 
 
• The Volt is the SI unit of electric potential, electric potential difference, and electromotive force.
 
• Named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta, it measures the potential difference between two points.
 
• One Volt is defined as the potential difference that will drive one Ampere of current against one Ohm of resistance.
 
 
 
• **Metre (m)**
 
 
• The Metre is the SI unit of length.
 
• It is defined as the distance traveled by light in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.
 
• It is a fundamental unit in the metric system and is used to measure distance.

questions.question: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hyponatremia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hyponatremia is a condition where the sodium level in the blood is lower than normal.
 
• Sodium is an essential electrolyte that helps regulate water balance in and around cells.
 
• Common causes of hyponatremia include excessive fluid intake, certain medications, and conditions like heart failure or kidney disease.
 
• Symptoms of hyponatremia can range from mild (nausea, headache) to severe (confusion, seizures, coma).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyperkalemia**

 
 
• Hyperkalemia is a condition characterized by an abnormally high level of potassium in the blood.
 
• Potassium is crucial for normal cell function, especially in the heart, muscles, and nerves.
 
• Causes include kidney dysfunction, excessive potassium intake, and certain medications.
 
• Symptoms can include muscle fatigue, weakness, paralysis, and abnormal heart rhythms.
 
 
 
• **Hypokalemia**
 
 
• Hypokalemia is a condition where there is a lower than normal level of potassium in the blood.
 
• It can result from conditions like chronic kidney disease, excessive loss of potassium through urine, or inadequate potassium intake.
 
• Symptoms may include muscle cramps, weakness, fatigue, and cardiac arrhythmias.
 
• Treatment typically involves potassium supplements and addressing the underlying cause.
 
 
 
• **Hypernatremia**
 
 
• Hypernatremia is a condition where the sodium level in the blood is higher than normal.
 
• It often occurs due to dehydration, water loss, or excessive sodium intake.
 
• Symptoms can include thirst, confusion, muscle twitching, and, in severe cases, seizures or coma.
 
• Treatment focuses on slowly rehydrating the patient and addressing the cause of the sodium imbalance.

questions.question: Tera Tali folk dance is primarily associated with which of the following states?

The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tera Tali** is a unique and traditional folk dance form predominantly performed in the state of **Rajasthan**.
 
• This dance is a significant part of the culture of the **Kamar tribe** of Rajasthan.
 
• It involves the use of **manjiras** (small brass cymbals) tied to different parts of the body, especially the hands and feet.
 
• The performance is often accompanied by singing and is a reflection of the vibrant and rich cultural heritage of Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is known for its rich cultural heritage, historical forts, palaces, art, and traditional music and dance forms.
 
• Rajasthan is home to other famous folk dances like Ghoomar, Kalbelia, and Bhavai.
 
• The state's vibrant and colorful festivals like the Pushkar Camel Fair and the Jaipur Literature Festival attract tourists from all over the world.
 
 
 
• **Assam:**
 
 
• Assam is a state in northeastern India known for its tea plantations, wildlife, and the Brahmaputra River.
 
• Bihu is the most important and widely celebrated festival in Assam, involving traditional dance and music.
 
• The state is also known for its rich biodiversity and is home to the Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh:**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is located in central India and is often referred to as the "Heart of India" due to its geographical location.
 
• The state has a rich cultural history and is known for its historical sites like Khajuraho, Bhimbetka rock shelters, and Sanchi Stupa.
 
• Folk dances like Gaur, Phulpati, and Maanch are popular in Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Haryana:**
 
 
• Haryana is a state in northern India, known for its agricultural prosperity and as the home of the Green Revolution.
 
• The state is known for traditional folk dances like Jhumar, Dhamal, and Phag.
 
• Haryana has a rich history and is known for its contributions to Indian sports, especially wrestling and kabaddi.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Vakil under the reign of Mughal Emperor, Akbar, who received the title of Khan-i-Khanan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bairam Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bairam Khan was a prominent noble and general of the Mughal Empire during the reign of Emperor Akbar.
 
• He served as the regent and guardian of young Akbar, managing the affairs of the state and the military.
 
• Bairam Khan was conferred with the title of "Khan-i-Khanan," which means "Khan of Khans" or "Chief of Chiefs."
 
• His loyalty and strategic expertise were instrumental in consolidating Mughal rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vakil:** The term "Vakil" in the Mughal administration refers to a representative or a high-ranking official who acted on behalf of the emperor. The Vakil was responsible for supervising the administration and ensuring that the emperor's orders were implemented.
 
• **Khan-i-Khanan:** This title was one of the highest honors in the Mughal hierarchy, bestowed upon individuals who demonstrated exceptional loyalty and service to the emperor. It signified supreme authority and respect.
 
• **Akbar's Reign:** Akbar, also known as Akbar the Great, was the third Mughal emperor who ruled from 1556 to 1605. His reign is noted for significant administrative, cultural, and military achievements, including the establishment of a centralized government and promoting a policy of religious tolerance.
 
• **Birbal and Raja Todar Mal:** While Birbal was one of Akbar's trusted advisors and known for his wit and wisdom, Raja Todar Mal served as Akbar's finance minister and played a crucial role in the implementation of revenue reforms. Neither of them held the title of "Khan-i-Khanan."
